title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: directors, employees and contractors
tiers.description: All directors of New Hope Corporation Limited, employees of the Group (the Company and any entity it controls) and contractors (including consultants and advisers) engaged by the Group from time to time. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test and any direction from the Company not to deal, but not by the Trading Window, pre-approval, short-term, short selling, hedging, stock lending or margin lending restrictions, which are expressed to apply only to Restricted Personnel and their Associates.

tiers.name: Restricted Personnel
tiers.description: The directors and all key management personnel; any member of the Group Executive Team; any employee or contractor in the Finance, Legal or Corporate Development teams; any General Manager or Finance employee at a business unit or operation who regularly has access to price sensitive information; any employee or contractor designated by the Chair of the Board or the CEO and notified by the Company Secretary; any executive assistant to any of the above; and (by paragraph 4.1(g)) their Associates. Subject to pre-approval for every dealing, the Trading Windows, and the section 9 prohibitions.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel of the Company, a subset of Restricted Personnel. Distinguished only for approval (the Chair of the Board, or in his or her absence two directors; for the Chair, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee or a non-executive director) and for the obligation to notify the Company Secretary of any dealing within 24 hours.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Personnel in his or her dealings with the Company or Company securities (including spouse or partner, children and dependents), and any company or other entity which the Restricted Personnel has an ability to control. Named within the definition of Restricted Personnel, so they carry the same restrictions; the Restricted Personnel must obtain clearance for their dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities (such as options or share rights) including hedging or similar arrangements

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company Secretary, in consultation with the Chair of the Board or the Chief Executive Officer, may prohibit certain or all Restricted Personnel from dealing during a Trading Window or an ad hoc Trading Window, notifying them without needing to provide a reason. Separately, Restricted Personnel and their Associates must not deal when directed not to do so by the Chair of the Board, the CEO or the Company Secretary, even in a Trading Window, and any director, employee or contractor must not deal once the Company notifies them not to, for a specified period or until further notice.

rules.detail: Effects-based ban with no vesting, tier, venue or approval qualification. It reaches both Securities held and entitlements to acquire Securities such as options or share rights, and the words 'or similar arrangements' close off economically equivalent structures. Notably, the excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 relieve only paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b), 9.1(c) and section 7, not paragraph 9.2, so there is no exemption at all.
rules.evidence: Restricted Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into: (a) transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities (such as options or share rights) including hedging or similar arrangements;

rules.detail: Section 9 is expressed to bind only Restricted Personnel and their Associates. A director, employee or contractor who is not Restricted Personnel is not caught by the hedging, stock lending or margin lending prohibitions, although the definition of Restricted Personnel captures every director and all key management personnel, so the gap is confined to junior staff and contractors.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy apply only to Restricted Personnel and their Associates.

rules.detail: There is no free-standing derivatives clause. A purchased put and a written call over New Hope shares are transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of Securities, so both legs of a collar are prohibited. A derivative that did not limit economic risk is not expressly banned but would still be a dealing requiring pre-approval and would have to pass the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities (such as options or share rights) including hedging or similar arrangements;

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar loans are not named. Any such structure limits the economic risk of Securities and so falls within 9.2(a), and where it is funded against the shares it is also an arrangement similar to margin lending under 9.2(b). Only an outright sale, pre-approved and inside a Trading Window, achieves liquidity.
rules.evidence: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;

rules.detail: Flat ban at any time, undefined. The excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 are expressed to override this paragraph, so passive or plan dealings are not treated as short selling.
rules.evidence: Restricted Personnel and their Associates must not at any time: ... (c) engage in short-selling of Securities.

rules.detail: Stock lending is named and prohibited outright, with no approval route. This matters for a collar because banks commonly expect to borrow or rehypothecate the collateral shares.
rules.evidence: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over New Hope Securities is a financial product that operates to limit or invert economic risk and so is caught by 9.2(a); a short CFD also engages the short selling ban and any in-and-out position the three-month short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities

rules.detail: Margin lending in relation to Securities is prohibited outright for Restricted Personnel and their Associates. There is no consent, materiality or grandfathering carve-out and no rules about margin calls or forced sales, because the arrangement cannot exist in the first place.
rules.evidence: Restricted Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into: ... (b) stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge or a pledge is not named and is not part of the definition of dealing. However, pledging Securities to a lender to support a loan is on any sensible reading an arrangement 'similar' to margin lending in relation to Securities and so falls within 9.2(b). A charge unconnected with any borrowing is genuinely unaddressed.
rules.evidence: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;

rules.detail: Unlike many ASX policies there is no express catch-all banning 'any other secured financing arrangement'. The prohibition is framed as 'stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities', but a limited-recourse or collar loan secured on New Hope shares, with loan-to-value triggers and a lender sale right, is materially the same arrangement as a margin loan and would be treated as caught. There is no approval route in any event.
rules.evidence: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;

rules.detail: Paragraph 9.2 binds only Restricted Personnel and their Associates, so an employee or contractor outside that group who borrows against Company securities is not covered. Every director and all key management personnel are Restricted Personnel, so this gap is of no use to the executives a bank would be lending to.
rules.evidence: Restricted Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into:

rules.detail: Dealing for short term (less than three months) or speculative gain is prohibited at any time. The excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 (plan participation, DRP, SPP, rights issue, takeover acceptance, no change in beneficial interest, pre-approved non-discretionary trading plans) are expressly excluded from this paragraph.
rules.evidence: Restricted Personnel and their Associates must not at any time: ... (b) deal in Securities for short term (less than three months) or speculative gain;

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board, or in his or her absence two directors; for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee or in his or her absence a non-executive director. Requests are submitted to the Company Secretary (or their delegate), who forwards them to the approver.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (notification of any dealing in the Company's securities, to assist the Company comply with its ASX Listing Rule disclosure obligations)
clearance.evidence: If approval to deal is granted, the Restricted Personnel will be notified in writing (which may include notification via email) and in each circumstance the duration of the approval will be two business days.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (or their delegate) for all Restricted Personnel other than key management personnel and the Chair of the Board
clearance.evidence: The approver may: (a) grant or refuse the request; and (b) impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion. The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

clearance.approver: The same approver as for the Restricted Personnel to whom they are associated; the Restricted Personnel must obtain the clearance on their behalf
clearance.evidence: Restricted Personnel must take appropriate steps to ensure that their “Associates” only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Personnel to whom they are associated with would be permitted to deal under this Policy. For example, by obtaining clearance in accordance with this Policy in respect of the Associates’ dealings.
Restricted Personnel and their Associates must seek approval to deal in Company securities prior to dealing in the Company’s securities.

short_term.basis: dealing for short term (less than three months) or speculative gain
carve_outs: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company
acquisition through a dividend reinvestment plan, a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders, or a rights issue
disposal through acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities
trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan
short_term.evidence: deal in Securities for short term (less than three months) or speculative gain;

exceptions.evidence: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company. However, where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy;

acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue;
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the employee or director is a beneficiary);

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the employee, director or contractor did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the employee, director or contractor to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board, two directors, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, a non-executive director or the Company Secretary (per paragraph 7.2)
exceptions.evidence: In exceptional circumstances, Restricted Personnel and their Associates may deal in securities outside a Trading Window with approval under section 7 ... Exceptional circumstances may exist where, for example: (a) the person is suffering severe financial hardship;
the person is required to trade by a court order, enforceable court undertaking or other legal requirement;
other exceptional circumstances exist, as determined by the person considering the approval.

external_documents: Employee, executive and director equity plan rules operated by the Company
exemption_authority: Approval to deal, including outside a Trading Window in exceptional circumstances, is given by the Chair of the Board (or in his or her absence two directors) for key management personnel, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (or a non-executive director) for the Chair of the Board, and the Company Secretary or their delegate for all other Restricted Personnel. The approver may refuse without reasons, impose conditions and revoke at any time, and will not approve a dealing that fails the Front Page Test. No one has authority to exempt anyone from the paragraph 9.2 hedging, stock lending and margin lending prohibitions: the excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 are expressed to relieve only paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b), 9.1(c) and section 7.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into: (a) transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities (such as options or share rights) including hedging or similar arrangements;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The test is economic effect and expressly includes 'similar arrangements', so a put and call collar over vested New Hope shares is prohibited regardless of venue, structure or vesting status.

bespoke_clauses.topic: stock lending and margin lending banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing leg is also blocked, and the express ban on stock lending forecloses the rehypothecation and borrow arrangements a bank would ordinarily rely on for the collateral.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following circumstances ... are therefore excluded from the operation of paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b) and 9.1(c) and section 7 of this Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The excluded dealings list is drafted to relieve the Trading Window, approval, short-term and short selling rules but deliberately not the hedging and margin lending prohibitions in 9.2, which therefore admit of no exception at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted personnel for the purposes of this policy are ... (g) a family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Personnel ... and any companies or any other entity which the Restricted Personnel has an ability to control (Associates).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Associates are not merely subject to a look-through duty, they are themselves Restricted Personnel, so a spouse's trust or a controlled company cannot enter the collar or the loan either.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Personnel and their Associates must not at any time: (a) deal in Securities when directed not to do so by the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer or the Company Secretary (even if in a Trading Window);
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Three individuals can each block any dealing at any moment without reasons, so no execution or unwind date can be treated as certain.

bespoke_clauses.topic: windows can be closed without reason
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary, in consultation with the Chair of the Board or Chief Executive Officer of the Company, may also prohibit certain or all Restricted Personnel from dealing in Company Securities during a Trading Window or an ad hoc Trading Window. Where Restricted Personnel are prohibited, the Company Secretary will notify them and does not need to provide a reason.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a scheduled window is not a reliable execution period, and the executive cannot explain a cancellation to a counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval to deal is granted ... in each circumstance the duration of the approval will be two business days. ... The approver ... may revoke their approval at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be priced and executed within two business days and remains revocable throughout, which no negotiated bilateral structure could reliably meet.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive is barred from telling the bank why the transaction cannot proceed, so documentation needs a no-reasons termination right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An optics veto sits over every approval, and a director monetising a stake through a bank structure is exactly the kind of transaction that would fail it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Personnel who are aware of information that they suspect might increase or decrease the market price for the Company's Securities if it were announced must explain this when seeking approval to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The applicant carries an affirmative disclosure burden beyond a clean insider trading representation, which increases the chance of refusal for a large structured trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action, including compulsory divestment of the securities, forfeiture of securities and/or summary dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can lead to compulsory divestment or forfeiture of the very shares pledged, which is a direct credit risk for a secured lender.

bespoke_clauses.topic: plan shares fall back under the policy
bespoke_clauses.clause: where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vested plan shares are fully subject to the hedging and margin lending prohibitions, so there is no free pool of collateral once shares leave the plan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Paragraph 9.2(b) prohibits 'stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities' but contains no express catch-all for 'any other secured financing arrangement'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only conceivable argument for a collar loan is that it is not 'similar' to margin lending, but that argument fails in any event because 9.2(a) independently prohibits the option legs.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any New Hope director or executive. Paragraph 9.2(a) prohibits Restricted Personnel and their Associates from entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of Securities or entitlements to acquire Securities, including hedging or similar arrangements, which captures both the purchased put and the written call irrespective of venue or vesting state, and paragraph 9.2(b) separately prohibits stock lending, margin lending or similar arrangements in relation to Securities, which covers the loan secured on the collared shares. Every director and all key management personnel are Restricted Personnel, their Associates (spouse, dependants, controlled entities) are themselves defined as Restricted Personnel, and the excluded dealings in paragraph 12.1 are drafted to relieve only paragraphs 5.1, 6.1, 9.1(b), 9.1(c) and section 7, so paragraph 9.2 has no exception and no approver can waive it. Even an outright sale is tightly controlled: pre-approval is required for every dealing, approval lasts two business days, may be refused or revoked at any time without reasons, must be kept confidential if refused, and will not be granted where the dealing fails the Front Page Test. Breach can result in compulsory divestment or forfeiture of the securities as well as summary dismissal.
